stories.notes: Story has empty acceptance criteria and no existing spec. Cross-platform (GO, UP, MX) live preview feature is complex — involves real-time content rendering, state management, and multi-platform concerns. openspec must run first to elaborate requirements and draft acceptance criteria from scratch; speckit then hardens with testability criteria, security checks (preview data isolation, auth for preview endpoints), and edge cases (concurrent sessions, content state sync).

agentContributions.notes: Novel capability — Contentstack Live Preview does not exist anywhere in the codebase. The ContentstackProvider is the single content source for 236+ consumers via useContent, making it the attachment point. VCs derived from description since ACs are empty. External Contentstack services are unreachable at test time, so criteria stop at our boundary: what our code subscribes to, how it handles events/responses, and what it renders given known data.

Openspec provided zero ACs, noting this is a novel capability. I synthesized all criteria from the story title, the identified attachment points (ContentstackProvider, useContent, ContentstackLink), and standard Contentstack Live Preview behavior patterns. Key design decisions: (1) AC-1/2/3 cover the happy-path update flow from provider through hook to component; (2) AC-4/5/6/7 cover resilience and graceful degradation since the live preview service is external and unreliable; (3) AC-8/9/12 cover security/environment gating to prevent preview leaking to production; (4) AC-10 is an explicit non-regression gate for the 236+ existing consumers; (5) AC-11 addresses a data-integrity edge case where mismatched preview events could corrupt the wrong consumer's state. CAVEAT: I could not read the actual source files (contentstackContext.tsx, useContent.ts, contentCard.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx), so my criteria are based on inference from file names and standard Contentstack SDK patterns. The actual data shapes, hook signatures, or provider architecture may require adjustments to these criteria. If the existing useContent hook returns data in a specific shape (e.g., contentCard interface), the preview merge behavior should preserve that exact shape — this should be verified against source.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: All four declared manifest paths exist and are resolved across all three codelines (gotransit, upexpress, metrolinx) with zero unresolved entries. The context file has case/extension variants per codeline but every variant is explicitly resolved. Verification criteria are seven observable, boundary-scoped behavioral checks covering text/image/link/card live updates, graceful degradation when preview is unavailable, production isolation, and card list reordering — all testable without external Contentstack services. Agent collaboration was complementary and non-overlapping: openspec correctly identified this as a novel capability, scoped criteria to our code boundary, and located the ContentstackProvider/useContent attachment point; speckit then hardened with resilience, security/environment gating, non-regression coverage for 236+ existing consumers, and data-integrity edge cases. Empty acceptanceCriteria array with acceptanceChanged=false is expected brownfield redaction per pipeline policy and not a defect. Speckit's caveat about not reading source files does not lower the score per review guidelines.
